pages.text: Snow crunches under paws as Willa the wolf trots through a pine forest, nose low, reading the smells on the wind.
Willa is a mammal with thick fur. Fur helps wolves stay warm when the weather is cold.
She meets her family pack. Packs work together, sharing care for pups and watching for danger.
A long howl rises into the air. Howls help wolves communicate across distance in forests and valleys.
Willa also uses body posture—ears, tail, and stance—to show feelings like calm, alert, or playful.
Tracks in the snow tell a story. The pack follows carefully, using quiet steps and sharp senses.
Wolves are carnivores, and they hunt together. Working as a team helps them catch food safely.
After the search, the pack rests in a sheltered spot. Rest helps them save energy for later.
Before sunset, Willa checks on the pups. Packs care for young ones so they can grow strong.
Night falls quietly. Willa curls her tail around her body, warm in her fur, listening to the forest’s sleepy sounds.
